chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who has intercourse with a beast, or a sheep, or a camel, or a cow. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is that he be whipped a penalty (hadd) that is not the complete penalty (hadd). Then he would be exiled from one land to another. And they mentioned that the flesh of that beast is prohibited, along with its milk.'

key_terms.بَهِيمَةً: Beast or animal (general term for livestock)
key_terms.حَدّاً: A fixed legal penalty prescribed by Sharia
key_terms.غَيْرَ الْحَدِّ: Not the complete/standard penalty; a lesser or distinct punishment
key_terms.يُنْفَى: Exiled or banished from a place

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment and ruling for the meat of the animal in cases of bestiality according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifies a distinct penal code for bestiality, prescribing a partial flogging (ghayr al-hadd) followed by exile, reflecting the juristic view that it is a major sin but distinct from adultery. The prohibition extends to the meat and milk of the specific animal involved, emphasizing the ritual impurity or sanctity associated with the act. This ruling highlights the practical application of hadd penalties in early Shia jurisprudence as recorded in al-Kafi.
